prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: Who Gives A Crap (company_id who-gives-a-crap; category: recycled and bamboo toilet paper)
Official domains: whogivesacrap.org
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://eu.whogivesacrap.org/pages/about-us | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"We're here to uncrap the world Young smiling boy standing in front of colourful stack of Who Gives A Crap recycled toilet paper playfully throwing toilet paper roll at camera. Who Gives A Crap premium toiler paper black and white packaging sitting on bathroom shelf with hand reaching to grab single roll What we're about"

[P2] source: https://eu.whogivesacrap.org/pages/about-us | document: official_domain | type: brand_positioning | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Doing good without compromises Ready for a bummer? Every day, 1 million trees are cut down to make traditional toilet paper. That's why we make our rolls from recycled fibres or bamboo. But just because it's eco, doesn't mean it's crap. The stuff you buy should work well, look good and not destroy the planet. We've made it our business (literally) to create the softest, strongest, most delightful eco-friendly products at an affordable price. And not to toot our own horn, but we've done a really good job. Ok, toot toot. Check it out How we got here"

[P3] source: https://alli.pmg.com/customer-story/who-gives-a-crap/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Our media strategy used host-read branded segments with influential podcasters such as The Guilty Feminist, Katherine Ryan, and Off Menu, among others; and 4-6 weeks-long activations across the full digital and print ecosystem of The Guardian, a hugely popular publisher with reach in the U.K. and Australia, to authentically express WGAC's compelling brand values. We also extended the campaign's longevity in-market through TVC cutdowns running across YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram, with paid social amplification of creator content and data-led OOH placements near select stores and retailers with WGAC toilet paper on their shelves, nudging consumers towards potential points of purchase."

[P4] source: https://alli.pmg.com/customer-story/who-gives-a-crap/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Building global awareness to wipe out the sanitation crisis Who Gives A Crap makes eco-friendly toilet paper and gives 50% of profits to help bring sanitation to the 2.4 billion people without a toilet. After 10 years of growth through word of mouth, it needed its first global brand campaign to support retail expansion in the U.K. and Australia. With Alli, PMG refined the audience into \"Uncrappers,\" people who want easy ways to do the right thing, and gave every market and partner the same audience definition. Broadcast, TikTok creators, podcasts, The Guardian, and out-of-home near stockists carried the brand's playful tone in both countries."

[P5] source: https://alli.pmg.com/customer-story/who-gives-a-crap/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"And between the social creator content and paid social amplification, WGAC saw 54.2 million video views on TikTok alone, with over 609k engagements (and 12k new followers) across the United Kingdom and Australia. Alli Brand Equity tied these movements in awareness, ad recall, and consideration back to media exposure and the Uncrapper personas built in Audience Planner, giving WGAC a clear read on which channels and moments moved the needle hardest and where to press next as retail expansion continues. While WGAC grew through word of mouth, our team was able to help the brand evolve through its first-ever global brand campaign, and inspire change in consumers' attitudes and behaviors."

[P6] source: https://canvasbusinessmodel.com/blogs/target-market/who-gives-a-crap-target-market | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | flags: vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics | dates in text: 2025 | published: unknown
"How Does Who Gives a Crap Win & Keep Customers? Who Gives A Crap acquires customers through high-impact digital storytelling and a referral-led growth engine that treats introductions as a functional bridge from curiosity to purchase. In 2025 the brand's 'Refer a Friend' program drove 25% of new signups, while viral Instagram and TikTok unboxing content-often organic-amplified reach without heavy ad spend. SEO/SEM targeting queries like \"sustainable toilet paper\" grew 40% year-over-year, capturing intent at the top of the funnel. Retention hinges on a data-driven subscription model and CRM automation that turns transactions into partnerships."

"And between the social creator content and paid social amplification, WGAC saw 54.2 million video views on TikTok alone, with over 609k engagements (and 12k new followers) across the United Kingdom and Australia. "It all started with 50 hours on a toilet and a dream Actually, it started when we learned billions of people don't have access to clean water or a toilet. It's devastating, it's dangerous and we knew we had to do something about it. That's when we created our unique business model - 50% of profits donated to help the billions of people in need. Crowdfunding for our first production run, our CEO Simon sat on a toilet for 50 hours until we successfully reached our $50,000 goal. Since then, we've made a whole lot of toilet paper, added new products to our line up, donated millions and grown our community of people passionate about making the world a better place."
